Judgment:

1. This is a claim for compensation arising out of the Detailed Accident Report filed u/s 158(6)
Motor Vehicle Act, qua petitioner Ajay Tiwari, Mrs. Pooja Tiwari, Abhi Tiwari, Payal and Amir Prasad for the injuries suffered by them in a vehicular accident which occurred on 08.08.2019 with respect to which FIR No. 487/19 was registered at Police Station Mehrauli against R-1 Sanjeev Kumar, driver of the offending vehicle.

The same is treated as petition under Section u/s 166 and 140 MV Act.
2.
The IO has filed copies of the criminal proceedings including FIR and the charge-sheet in the DAR.
3. It is pertinent to mention here that IO in his chargesheet has mentioned that the injured Payal and Amir Prasad could not be traced out despite various efforts.
The addresses on their MLCs were also incomplete.

4. Brief facts of the vehicular accident as averred in the DAR are that on 08.08.2019 at about 7.30 AM complainant Ajay Tiwari alongwith his wife Pooja Tiwari and Son Kartik Tiwari @ Abhi Tiwari were travelling in the Eeco Car bearing no. DL- 3CBC-9470 for going towards Gurgaon.

The driver of the vehicle Ajay Tiwari and ors. vs. Sanjeev Kumar and ors.
was driving it in a very rash and negligent manner.

At about 7.30 AM when they reached near Andheria mod Gurugram Mehrauli road, suddenly the driver of the vehicle who was driving in a very high speed, took a sharp turn due to which vehicle turned turtle.
Due to the impact, they received grievous injuries alongwith other passengers.
5. At the time of filing of the DAR, the driver / respondent no. 1 Sanjeev appeared alongwith the owner of the vehicle who was also his real brother.
However, thereafter they stopped appearing and were proceeded ex-parte by my Ld. Predecessor vide order dated 10.03.2022.

6. The insurance company, however resisted the case of the petitioners by filing the detailed written statement stating that the insured vehicle was private vehicle but it was being used for hire and reward and hence there is a violation of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

However, it is admitted that vehicle was insured with the respondent vide policy bearing no. M7406271 valid from 23.04.2019 to 22.04.2020 in the name of the insured.

sentences.text: It is a settled legal position that while deciding a petition u/s 166 of the M V Act, the Claims Tribunal has to decide negligence on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.

Reference in this regard is made to the observations of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Kaushnumma Begum and Others v/s New India Assurance Company Limited, 2001 ACJ 421 SC, wherein it was held that the issue of wrongful act or omission on the part of the driver of motor vehicle involved in the accident is of secondary importance and mere use or involvement of motor vehicle in causing bodily injuries or death to a human being or damage to property would make the petition maintainable u/s 166 & 140 of the M V Act.

The petitioners in their affidavits Ex.PW1/A and Ex.PW2/A have clearly deposed that the driver of the offending vehicle was driving it rashly and negligently.
The testimony of PW2 fully supported the version of the PW1.
Their testimony is uncontroverted and unrebutted.
As already observed, the entire investigation conducted by the IO also support the version of the petitioner.

22. Further, it is pertinent to note that the respondent no. 1/ driver of the aforesaid vehicle was the material witness to throw light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances, the accident had taken place.
However, he has preferred not to enter into the witness box during the course of the inquiry.
Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle.
The driver did not enter into the witness box to controvert the claim of the petitioners or even to explain the circumstances of accident.
The evidence led by petitioners is unrebutted and un-controverted.

23. On the basis of evidence on record, above observation and Ajay Tiwari and ors. vs. Sanjeev Kumar and ors.
discussion it is proved that the abovesaid accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of R1 Sanjeev Kumar due to which the injured received injuries.

Herein, Section 150 of the MV Act has to be referred which provides as under:-
150. Duty of insurers to satisfy judgments and awards against persons insured in respect of third party risks - (1) If, after a certificate of insurance has been issued under sub-section (3) of section 147 in favour of the person by whom a policy has been effected, judgment or award in respect of any such liability as is required to be covered by a policy under clause (b) of sub-section (1) of section 147 (being a liability covered by the terms of the policy) or under the provisions of section 164 is obtained against any person insured by the policy, then, notwithstanding that the insurer may be entitled to avoid or cancel or may have avoided or cancelled the policy, the insurer shall, subject to the provisions of this section, pay to the person entitled to the benefit of the award any sum not exceeding the sum assured payable thereunder, as if that person were the decree holder, in respect of the liability, together with any amount payable in respect of costs and any sum payable in respect of interest on that sum by virtue of any enactment relating to interest on judgments.

(2)No sum shall be payable by an insurer under sub-section (1) in respect of any judgment or award unless, before the commencement of the proceedings in which the judgment or award is given the insurer had notice through the court or, as the case may be, the Claims Tribunal of the bringing of the proceedings, or in respect of such Ajay Tiwari and ors. vs. Sanjeev Kumar and ors.
judgment or award so long as its execution is stayed pending an appeal; and an insurer to whom notice of the bringing of any such proceedings is so given shall be entitled to be made a party thereto, and to defend the action on any of the following grounds, namely: -

sentences.text: COMPENSATION FOR THE INJURED AJAY TIWARI 29.
In the present case, the injured Ajay Tiwari has sustained grievous injury and as per Discharge note Ex.PW1/2 he was diagnosed with "Soft Tissue Injury".
He was admitted in AIIMS on 08.08.2019 and discharged on the same date.
He has sustained 3% disability in his left upper limb.
The petitioner has placed on record medical bills of Rs.2,009/-.
Thereafter, he took the treatment from the AIIMS Hospital as Outdoor Patient.
Due to the accidental injury, the injured must have suffered mental agony and pain and the injured must have visited hospital while arranging some cab/ auto to visit the hospital.
Further, injured has stated that he was doing private work and was earning Rs. 20,000/- per month.
However, he has not brought any document on record in regard to his income and employment.
On perusal of the testimony of PW1, it is found that in his affidavit he stated that he was doing some private job whereas in his cross- examination he stated that he was working as a carpenter.

Therefore, looking into the injuries sustained by the injured Ajay Tiwari, I award him a lumpsum amount of compensation of Rs. 2,50,000/- alongwith 9% interest per annum from the date of filing the claim petition till its realization.
The entire amount is directed to be released to the petitioner/ Injured Ajay Tiwari.

It is a settled legal position that while deciding a petition u/s 166 of the M V Act, the Claims Tribunal has to decide negligence on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
This court is of the opinion that a lumpsum amount of compensation of Rs.25000/- would be proper and just for the injury suffered by Ajay Tiwari and ors. vs. Sanjeev Kumar and ors.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
However, he has preferred not to enter into the witness box during the course of the inquiry.
Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle.
The driver did not enter into the witness box to controvert the claim of the petitioners or even to explain the circumstances of accident.
The evidence led by petitioners is unrebutted and un-controverted.
First of all the court has to decide as to whom the liability to pay the compensation is fastened.
Hence the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation.
In the present case, it has been duly proved that the offending vehicle was being used by respondent no. 1 for commercial purposes without permit.
Thus, the respondent no(s). 1 and 2 are liable to pay the compensation for the rash and negligent act of the respondent no. 1 and wrongful action of the respondent no. 2.

in this award and shall have the right to recover the same from respondent No(s). 1 and 2 jointly and severally.
In the present case, the injured Ajay Tiwari has sustained grievous injury and as per Discharge note Ex.PW1/2 he was diagnosed with "Soft Tissue Injury".
He was admitted in AIIMS on 08.08.2019 and discharged on the same date.
He has sustained 3% disability in his left upper limb.

She has sustained 3% disability in her right lower limb.
Due to the accidental injury, the injured must have suffered mental agony and pain and the injured must have visited hospital while arranging some cab/ auto to visit the hospital.
In the present case, the injured Kartik Tiwari @ Abhi Tiwari was minor at the time of accident.
